segs: SailPoint sells two products that do the
same job, IdentityIQ and Identity
Security Cloud. So, which one should you
learn? And which one should your company
run? Here is the difference in under 3
minutes.
Think of it like a home. IdentityIQ is a
house you own. Identity Security Cloud
is a serviced apartment you rent. Both
keep you safe. What changes is who does
the work.
First, what is the same? Both collect
accounts from your applications. Both
build one identity for every person. And
both grant access, review access, and
remove it when someone leaves.
Difference one, who runs it? IdentityIQ
is software you install. Your servers,
your database, your upgrades. Identity
Security Cloud is a service. SailPoint
runs it, and updates arrive on their
own. To reach systems inside your
network, it uses a small connector
called a virtual appliance.
Difference two, how much you can change.
In your own house, you can knock down
any wall. IdentityIQ lets you write
custom rules, workflows, and forms for
almost anything. In the apartment, you
can decorate, but the walls stay where
they are. The cloud gives you
transforms, workflows, and a small set
of approved rules. Less freedom, but far
less to maintain.
Difference three, where new features
land. The newest AI features, like
requesting access through chat, are
landing in the cloud. But the house is
not being abandoned. On October 6th,
SailPoint announced IdentityIQ 9.0, a
rebuilt foundation, a refreshed
interface, access with a start and an
end time, and a tool that automates most
of the upgrade. In SailPoint's words, no
customer is left behind.
One warning about names. Identity
Security Cloud used to be called
Identity Now, and SailPoint's newest
announcements call the cloud side Human
Fabric. An application in IdentityIQ is
called a source in the cloud. Different
labels, same ideas.
So, which one? Choose Identity IQ if you
have strict data rules or years of
custom logic. Choose the cloud if you
want speed and no servers to look after.
And if you're learning, learn the
concepts: aggregation, provisioning,
certification. They work the same way in
both.
Which one does your company run? Tell me
in the comments.
